correctness.rationale: SPD A=I+vv^T, exact block-Jacobi P=blockdiag(I+v_j v_j^T); S=P^-1/2 A P^-1/2. Active block spike directions reduce S to H with H_ii=1 and H_ij=sqrt(q_i q_j/[(1+q_i)(1+q_j)]); all perpendicular eigenvalues are 1, so extreme eigenvalues come from H for positive active blocks. Two blocks have eigenvalues 1±sqrt(xy/[(1+x)(1+y)]) and κ(S)<=1+x+y, equality x=y. In (s,s,t) three-active-block family the antisymmetric eigenvalue is 1/(1+s), other eigenvalues (2+3s±sqrt(Delta))/(2(1+s)), Delta=s²+8st(1+s)/(1+t). Delta−9s²=8s(t−s)/(1+t) selects min eigenvalue. Symbolic exact factorizations of Delta−(s+2t)² and Delta(K+1)²−(2+3s)²(K−1)² prove deterioration iff t<s or s<t<s(4s+3)/(s+1), with equality at t=s and second threshold. Independent exact symbolic positive-sum certificate proves ratio strictly below 3/2 and asymptotic s=L²,t=L approaches 3/2. Direct generalized eigenproblem confirms witness κ=7+2sqrt6>10. No claim beyond (s,s,t) for the 3/2 constant or all SPD matrices.

value.rationale: An exact SPD preconditioner can strictly worsen the spectral condition number, with the first possible failure already at three active blocks. The complete deterioration/equality/improvement phase diagram and sharp 3/2 ceiling are natural diagnostic invariants for selecting a baseline preconditioner; they offer more actionable structure than a single counterexample or generic near-optimality bound.

limitations: The sign phase diagram assumes three strictly positive block energies (s,s,t) and exact Jacobi scaling.
No performance claim for sketched BLOKS, inexact factors, or solver wall clock.
